Rushes

Scroll through film trailers one at a time, see where each film is streaming, and decide what to watch tonight.

Visit the site ↗How to useIn motion

01

Problem

Choosing a film on a streaming service takes longer than it should. Each service shows only its own catalogue, the menus are rows of small posters, and finding out where a given film is available means leaving for another site.

02

What it does

Rushes shows one film per screen. The trailer plays as soon as the film arrives, and one scroll brings the next. For each film you choose Watch it, which saves it to a list, or Not for me, which hides it. A panel inside the app gives the services that carry the film in your country, the plot, a fact sheet, the cast and crew, more clips and similar films. A section for filmmakers adds lessons on structure, writing, cinematography, editing, sound, design, performance and producing.

03

How it is built

A single page with no framework. A Vercel function queries TMDB for films by year and genre, keeps those that have a trailer, and returns the trailer, credits, budget and streaming services in one response, so the API key never reaches the browser. Trailers play through the YouTube player, muted until the viewer turns the sound on. The list and the hidden films are stored on the device. Film data and images come from TMDB and streaming availability from JustWatch; Rushes is not endorsed by either.
